answer: One copper restores one unit of trading capacity; lagoon caps each identity at one unit and allows trading only while full. spiral ties key rotation to one operator, counts unretired identities \(k\), and sets every identity’s capacity leak to \(2^{k-1}\) units per epoch. Maintaining \(k\) heads therefore burns \(k2^{k-1}\) copper per epoch. A newcomer pays 1. Identity ten raises its operator’s bill from 2,304 to 5,120, adding 2,816. Fresh wallets, split payments and staggered refills cannot reduce that count-driven leak.
